changes.why: The data are an ongoing policy-tracking compilation of state Medicaid coverage (also held in CDC's STATE System), so surveillance/descriptive applies alongside the 2018–2022 comparison; states are the unit, which keeps ecologic.

equity.level_reason: Standard Medicaid enrollment (a low-income insurance group) defines the population; the Medicaid-versus-private smoking disparity is cited background and reducing disparities appears only as an implication, with no group-specific results.

level_alternative.reason: Insurance status only defines the population and the comparison is across years and states, so the disparity statements could be read as background with no equity analysis.

equity.equity_measurement: Insurance type (standard Medicaid) is the only SES proxy and defines the whole population; expansion enrollees are excluded and no results are given by enrollee characteristics.

notes: equity_action is set true because the report measures progress in a policy framed as reducing a Medicaid-related disparity against the Healthy People 2030 target; a stricter reading would call this monitoring. The HP2030 shortfall is a secondary fixed-referent comparison; the 2018–2022 pair stays primary. Laws and policies are named as explanations for coverage change, not for the disparity.
